newsitem.title: USA: Wash. 1,158 MW nuclear unit outage may begin Mar 1.
newsitem.headline: Wash. 1,158 MW nuclear unit outage may begin Mar 1.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) may ask the 1,158 megawatt (MW) WNP-2 nuclear power plant to begin its annual outage as early as Saturday, sources at the plant and BPA said Monday.

The plant is still officially scheduled to begin a 60-day refueling and maintenance outage on April 18, but there is a good chance it will begin earlier and last longer, a spokesman for Washington Public Power Supply System said.
"By the end of this week, we could be put into economic dispatch," he noted.
Economic dispatch refers to shutting a plant when its operating cost exceeds revenue from its power sales.
The nuclear unit has been operating below capacity since mid-January due to problems with an adjustable speed drive as well as the availability of lower-cost hydropower.
The unit was at 60 percent Monday morning after powering down to 25 percent on Sunday for work on its speed drives.
WNP-2 is expected to reach 90 percent capacity later Monday before again powering down to accomodate BPA's needs, the spokesman said.
